text:
alex: Heads-up — customer ACME reported 0.8% of structured_response payloads failing to parse in their downstream service. They started seeing it ~08:15 UTC and it's still happening.
maria: Do we have a sample from them? any error text? :thinking:
jordan: They sent a sample in the ticket: response body contains an extra trailing comma in "items" array, but our platform logs only show a 200 with content-type application/json+structured. No stacktrace in logs.
kevin: That's weird — if parsing failed client-side they'd still send us the original model output. Is there any transformation between model output and response body? e.g., templating, sanitization?
alex: We looked — the response pipeline runs redaction and then JSON normalization. Redaction can remove tokens and replace them with "[REDACTED]". The customer's failing example seems to have a redaction that removed the final object, leaving a dangling comma.
maria: So redaction can cause syntactically-invalid JSON. That seems like an edge-case. Why didn't our observability catch the broken JSON generation as an error?
jordan: Two gaps:
- request logs are redacted before being stored, so samples saved to S3 are already redacted and we can't see pre-redaction output
- our structured-output parsing metric only increments on the post-redaction validate step and we treat incorrect JSON as a non-fatal normalize warning (no alert)
kevin: Repro steps I ran locally:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Accept: application/json+structured" \
  -d '{"prompt":"generate items list with possible PII"}'
```
Sometimes the sanitizer replaces the last object with "[REDACTED]" leaving a trailing comma. Intermittent based on model output shape.
oncall-bot: Incident SUP-7421 created and linked to this thread. Priority: P2. Assigned: eng-platform + eng-ml.
alex: Short-term mitigation we can ship today: change redaction to remove the full object including preceding comma (i.e., collapse separators) instead of replacing inner text. That should avoid dangling commas.
maria: Longer term: add a pre-redaction sampling path that stores one in N unredacted model outputs in a secure vault accessible only to SRE/Support for debug. Also add a metric: structured_response.pre_redaction_invalid_count and alert if >0. We currently only count post-redaction warnings.
jordan: Action items:
  - eng-platform: implement comma-collapsing redactor (patch) — ETA 4h.
  - eng-ml: add validation that runs before redaction and increments metric and stores sample to secure store when sample rate triggers — ETA EOD.
  - support: ask ACME for a full failing HTTP request dump (headers + body) and CC privacy contact — maria
kevin: I'm going to instrument a dashboard query to show disparity between pre- and post-redaction validation rates once eng-ml ships the pre-redaction metric. Quick query (logs):
```
filter @message like /structured/ | stats count() by validation_status
```
alex: Also add correlation_id propagation: some of the requests from the customer go through their edge cache and we lose our x-redwood-cid header, making it impossible to join traces. We should fallback to logging model_request_id when cid missing.
maria: Noted. I'll file a follow-up RFC for trace propagation changes. For now I'll send ACME a recommended client-side tolerant parser snippet and ask them to retry once we deploy the sanitizer fix.
kevin: Patch merged to staging, running integration tests now. I'll push to canary and keep the thread updated.
alex: Thanks. If anyone from eng-ml or eng-platform wants to pair, ping me — I'll be on the call at 14:00 UTC to coordinate release and communications. :phone:
maria: tagging here so support can close the ticket after verification: @kevin please add the fix commit hash and canary timestamp.
kevin: Will do. commit: a1b2c3d, canary: 1991234588. Rolling to 10% first.
alex: Great. support to follow up with ACME after canary. Closing loop when they confirm parsing success. :thumbsup:
